episodes.167241: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours ahead of a cold front moving through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.167251: A few of strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours producing isolated wind damage.
episodes.167303: In the wake of a warm front passing overhead on the morning of May 3rd, daytime heating and brief periods of sunshine allowed southeast Ohio to become primed for afternoon thunderstorms. These storms arrived along a cold front, with several rounds occurring in Perry County. The first strong cell resulted in quarter to golf ball sized hail, while the second round brought damaging wind gusts. Downed trees and power lines were the main result from these strong winds.
episodes.167305: Warming temperatures and periods of sunshine on the afternoon of May 3rd aided in shower and thunderstorm development ahead of a cold front. Strong to severe storms passed through northern West Virginia that evening, with damaging wind gusts causing numerous downed trees and power lines across the area.
episodes.167338: Widespread pulse severe thunderstorms formed within a weak area of convergence across central South Carolina as the area remained positioned between an approaching shortwave and offshore ridge. Elevated instability, an inverted V sounding at low levels, and dry air aloft yielded an enhanced downburst and hail risk. Pulse convection produced severe winds and numerous hail reports across the area including a downburst in West Columbia.
episodes.167951: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms produce gusty winds over the coastal waters.
episodes.168120: A warm front lifted north into southwest Virginia sparking numerous showers and storms. Damaging winds and large hail accompanied these storms. The combination of robust instability and good shear helped the thunderstorms organize into a line as it progressed east into the Piedmont.
episodes.168154: An upper air disturbance caused heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms.  Early on in the episode, a flash flood occurred over a portion of Maui along Piilani Highway.  Otherwise, the precipitation produced small stream and drainage ditch flooding, and ponding on roadways, over other parts of Maui and on the Big Island.  No serious injuries were reported.
episodes.168216: Rainfall persisted across the area between April 28th and May 1st with three day totals over 3 inches between Edmunds, McPherson and Brown counties as well as upstream in North Dakota. This, combined with planned releases due to construction on the Elm Lake Spillway, resulted in minor flooding along the Elm River. Flooding was already occurring during the morning of May 1st and continued into May 2nd with a crest of 13.95 feet at the gauge near Frederick. The gauge at Westport went into flood stage on May 2nd, peaked in stage at 14.4 feet around mid day on May 4th, and then rapidly fell below flood stage on the morning of May 5th.
episodes.168326: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed and produced hail to ping pong balls in size.
episodes.168445: Heavy rain moved across much of northeast Illinois during the morning of May 3rd producing localized flooding.  Rainfall amounts were generally between 1 and 1.5 inches.
episodes.168587: As a surface low moved northeastward across northwestern Ohio and toward central Lake Erie, a warm front extending southeastward from the low moved northeastward toward northeast Ohio and northwest Pennsylvania, while the trailing cold front swept eastward across western Ohio during the early through mid-evening of the 3rd. A bow echo within the warm sector travelled northeastward across portions of northwestern and north-central Ohio. This bow echo generated damaging wind gusts, ping pong ball-size hail, and a couple QLCS tornadoes. The warm sector was characterized by weak to moderate MUCAPE, mixed layer LCL's less than 1000 meters AGL, moderate to strong effective bulk shear, and large surface-based ESRH near 150 meters squared per second squared.
episodes.168685: As a surface low moved northeastward across northwestern Ohio and toward central Lake Erie, a warm front extending southeastward from the low moved northeastward toward northeast Ohio and northwest Pennsylvania, while the trailing cold front swept eastward across western Ohio during the early through mid-evening of the 3rd. A line of multicell thunderstorms moved northeastward in the warm sector and produced a couple gale-force peak wind gusts along Sandusky Bay. These storms occurred in an environment comprised of weak to moderate MUCAPE and moderate to strong effective bulk shear.
episodes.168782: A shortwave trough over the Florida Panhandle and northeast Gulf moved over the area during the afternoon. At the surface, high pressure was centered just south of Bermuda with the ridge axis extending eastward across the FL/GA border. Light southerly flow enabled both Gulf and Atlantic coast sea breeze boundaries to move inland in the afternoon with pulse severe storms producing hail and gusty winds over a moist and unstable airmass, enhanced by the shortwave trough.
episodes.168783: A shortwave trough over the Florida Panhandle and northeast Gulf moved over the area during the afternoon. At the surface, high pressure was centered just south of Bermuda with the ridge axis extending eastward across the FL/GA border. Light southerly flow enabled both Gulf and Atlantic coast sea breeze boundaries to move inland in the afternoon with pulse severe storms producing hail and gusty winds over a moist and unstable airmass, enhanced by the shortwave trough.
episodes.168852: Numerous thunderstorms impacted the region during the afternoon and evening hours of May 3rd. Lift was be supported by a shortwave trough and a cold front crossing the Ohio Valley. Strong, deep shear and sufficient instability helped to maintain storms as they evolved from discrete storms in Ohio into a few more organized lines as they crossed Pennsylvania and northern West Virginia. Wind damage reports were fairly widespread across southwest Pennsylvania.  Although a tornado watch was issued, no tornadoes were reported in the region.
episodes.168853: Numerous thunderstorms impacted the region during the afternoon and evening hours of May 3rd. Lift was be supported by a shortwave trough and a cold front crossing the Ohio Valley. Strong, deep shear and sufficient instability helped to maintain storms as they evolved from discrete storms in Ohio into a few more organized lines as they crossed Pennsylvania and northern West Virginia. A few large hail reports were mixed in with several instances of wind damage.  Although a tornado watch was issued, no tornadoes  were reported in the area.
episodes.168854: Numerous thunderstorms impacted the region during the afternoon and evening hours of May 3rd. Lift was be supported by a shortwave trough and a cold front crossing the Ohio Valley. Strong, deep shear and sufficient instability helped to maintain storms as they evolved from discrete storms in Ohio into a few more organized lines as they crossed Pennsylvania and northern West Virginia. Several wind damage reports were received in northern West Virginia.  Although a tornado watch was issued, and one funnel cloud was spotted, no tornadoes were reported in the region.
episodes.169013: Scattered thunderstorms developed across southeast Georgia in the early afternoon hours within the large warm sector of a low pressure system centered near the Great Lakes. The thunderstorms produced large hail and damaging winds as they tracked eastward.
episodes.169014: Scattered thunderstorms developed across southeast Georgia in the early afternoon hours within the large warm sector of a low pressure system centered near the Great Lakes. The thunderstorms eventually moved into southeast South Carolina and produced large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.169067: Widespread showers and storms moved through the region during the evening hours of May 2nd into the early morning hours of May 3rd. An isolated severe storm moved through northern portions of the St. Louis metro area with damaging winds reported in St. Charles County.
episodes.169172: An isolated severe thunderstorm caused some tree damage in a part of Robeson County NC.
episodes.169360: A late season cold front brought a round of strong to severe storms across the area.  Two brief tornadoes occurred, one in Perry and the other in the St Marks Wildlife Refuge.
episodes.169367: A late season cold front brought a round of strong to severe storms across the area.
episodes.169413: Thunderstorms developed across northern Texas and eastern Oklahoma during the early morning hours of the 2nd, as a warm front approached the area from the south. The strongest storm produced damaging wind gusts in Choctaw County.||Thunderstorms redeveloped across portions of southeastern Oklahoma during the afternoon. Strong instability south of the warm front, combined with strong wind shear, supported an environment for supercell thunderstorms. One such storm produced a tornado and damaging wind in Le Flore County. ||Another round of severe thunderstorms, which developed along the dry line across central Oklahoma during the afternoon, moved through eastern Oklahoma during the evening in the form of a squall line. The strongest storms within this line produced damaging wind gusts and large hail up to quarter size. A brief tornado also occurred in Cherokee County.
episodes.169414: Thunderstorms developed across portions of southeastern Oklahoma and west central Arkansas during the afternoon of the 2nd. Strong instability south of a warm front, combined with strong wind shear, supported an environment for supercell thunderstorms. One such storm moved across Sebastian County, producing hail up to golf ball size and damaging wind gusts. ||Another round of severe thunderstorms that developed along the dry line across central Oklahoma during the afternoon moved through northwestern Arkansas during the evening in the form of a squall line. The strongest storms within this line produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.169415: A warm front passed through the Ohio Valley during the morning hours of May 3rd, with unstable air behind the warm front sparking clusters of showers and thunderstorms across central Kentucky during the afternoon hours before the surface cold front passed through.
episodes.169615: A line of storms developed along a cold front and pushed southeast through the region late in the evening of Monday May 2. A few warnings were issued near and north of the DFW Metroplex, but only one report of high winds was received.
episodes.169664: A dryline was the main focus for storm development during the afternoon of the 2nd as a compact upper wave crossed the area. Numerous storms led to reports of hail, high winds, and a few tornadoes through the afternoon and evening.
episodes.169746: Several rounds of moderate to heavy rainfall moved eastward across the region as a low pressure system developed over the southern high Plains and moved eastward into the Ozarks. Rainfall accumulations averaged between one half inch and one and a half inches, with isolated accumulations over two and a half inches along the Arkansas border.
episodes.169764: A stalled frontal zone was located over northeastern North Carolina and south-central Virginia during the day, while a lee surface trough was present over the Foothills of western North Carolina. A mid-level perturbation along with daytime heating led to the development of isolated to widely scattered showers and storms, starting over the western and central Piedmont in the mid to late afternoon, growing upscale into a line of storms and expanding into the Sandhills and southern Coastal Plain by the late afternoon and evening hours. Some of the stronger storms became severe and produced damaging winds and large hail. The storms moved east toward the coast and dissipated by late evening with the loss of daytime heating.
episodes.169793: A few rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms developed through May 5th. The bulk of the active weather took place from late on May 4th into the 5th as a cold front moved into the state from the northwest. In addition to severe weather reports of damaging wind and hail, very heavy rain fell from northeast Oklahoma eastward into Arkansas and across southern Missouri. This widespread heavy rain led to rises on area rivers as well as some flash flooding.
episodes.169868: Unstable air moved into portions of east central Indiana as a warm front and weak area of low pressure impacted the region. While several thunderstorms developed and remained below severe levels, a few storms produced precipitation loaded downdrafts and isolated wind damage.
episodes.169869: Unstable air moved into portions of east central Indiana as a warm front and weak area of low pressure impacted the region. The storms moved into northwestern Ohio, producing locally damaging winds and also some marginally severe hail.
episodes.169947: Storms moving through the Kansas City metro area produced some wind damage around Grandview.
episodes.169998: A storm developed and became severe in the evening, producing large hail.
episodes.170071: A cold front driven by gusty outflow winds moved through northern Utah, with a redevelopment of high winds behind the initial line across the West Desert.
episodes.170127: Heavy rains brought river flooding to portions of the Ouachita, Black, Spring, White, and Cache Rivers.
episodes.170178: Long-lasting showers and thunderstorms, due to the convergence of the land breeze with northeasterly winds along the Atlantic coastal waters, caused flash flooding across some areas between Vega Alta and Carolina just after midnight on May 3rd, 2022.
episodes.170234: Low pressure tracked from the Middle Mississippi Valley into the Ohio Valley on May 3 with a trailing warm front becoming stationary from western Virginia through south central Virginia and into northeast North Carolina. Meanwhile, high pressure was located off the Northeast coast allowing for easterly flow north of the front. Storms developed in southwest and south central Virginia as well as in North Carolina during the late afternoon, tracking into south central Virginia and northeast North Carolina into the evening before weakening.
episodes.170355: A dryline was the main focus for storm development during the afternoon of the 2nd as a compact upper wave crossed the area. Most of the storms were across Oklahoma but a few storms made it into western north Texas where a severe wind gust was recorded.
episodes.170394: Several thunderstorm wind gusts in excess of 60 mph were recorded on the afternoon of May 2nd.
episodes.170421: One report of storm damage was received from southern Indiana after an isolated severe storm formed in the warm sector of a low pressure system. The system passed west to east through central Illinois and Indiana, north of the reported damage.
episodes.170491: Scattered showers and thunderstorms affected Middle Tennessee on May 2 and again on May 3. A few reports of hail and damaging winds were received.

In Canonsburg, trees were reported to be blown down.

A few softwood and hardwood trees were snapped in this area, and a carport roof was lofted and deposited 100 feet downwind. This area marks the start of a locally enhanced swath of wind damage that continued to the Bradenton area.

Several hardwood and softwood trees were damaged in this area. A rooftop HVAC unit was displaced from its perch atop a single story school building. This area marks the eastern end of a locally enhanced swatch of wind damage that began in Loyalhanna.
Siding was blown off of a house in Bradenville.
Trees were reported to be blown down in Latrobe.
Several branches and whole trees snapped near the intersection of OH-18 and Gore Orphanage Road just west of Brighton.
Tree downed about two-miles north of Rochester.
Multiple power outages across extreme southern portions of Dinwiddie county.
Mesonet station just west of the northern tip of the Cedar Point Peninsula recorded a peak gust of 47 knots from a passing thunderstorm.
A mesonet station in Sandusky Bay, just north of Bay View, recorded a peak gust of 41 knots from a passing thunderstorm.
WeatherFlow site XTAM Tampa Bay Cut J reported a 51 mph wind gust.
Large trees limbs were down on the roadway.
One tree was blown down onto Adamsville Road.
One tree was blown down onto a local road in the town of Bridgeport.
